the design implication: optimizing a single badgir for individual building performance is the wrong unit of analysis. the correct unit is the array configuration — the spacing, orientation, and height distribution of badgirs across a city block or district — that produces the most favorable emergent urban wind pattern. traditional Yazd urban planners optimized this over generations through empirical iteration. computational fluid dynamics now allows this optimization to be run in simulation before construction.

## synthesis 6: generational pattern transmission across cultures (T2-RP11 × Track 1 global source taxonomy)

root pattern 11 (multi-channel generational pattern fidelity) is documented in Western secular science through two channels: behavioral (attachment theory) and biological (epigenetics). but the cross-cultural documentation of the same pattern predates the secular science by millennia:

— traditional Chinese medicine: the concept of "prenatal jing" (先天精) — essence transmitted from ancestors to offspring — is a different vocabulary for the same mechanism. the ancestral contribution to constitutional health is a core concept in TCM medical theory.

— Ayurvedic medicine: "beej dosha" (seed defect) — constitutional weaknesses transmitted through family lines that manifest predictably in offspring. the TKDL documentation of this concept spans centuries of Ayurvedic clinical observation.

— West African Yoruba tradition: the "ori" concept — the personal destiny that includes ancestral lineage as a constituent element of present identity.

— Indigenous North American traditions (across multiple cultures): the "seven generations" principle — responsibility extends seven generations forward because the mechanism of effect extends seven generations forward.

— biblical documentation: Exodus 20:5 "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation" — a structural observation about the transmission mechanism, not a theological prescription.

the convergence finding: when the same pattern is independently documented in Yoruba tradition, Chinese medicine, Ayurvedic medicine, Indigenous American philosophy, and biblical scripture — traditions that had no contact with each other for most of their development — the pattern is structural. the modern epigenetic science is not new knowledge about reality; it is the vocabulary in which Western science finally confirmed what every other major tradition had already observed.

the implication: the global non-Western knowledge record is not a collection of pre-scientific observations awaiting validation. it is a distributed observational archive of real mechanisms, documented in different vocabularies, that the mechanism-extraction protocol can translate into current scientific language and apply to current problems.

## synthesis 7: analog computing + Goodhart immunity (T1-IC8 × T2-RP17)

modern computational systems are vulnerable to measurement-target reflexive decoupling (root pattern 17): any system whose performance is measured by a metric will be optimized for the metric, decoupling the metric from the underlying reality. this applies to: AI systems optimized for measurable performance benchmarks that diverge from intended behavior; financial risk models optimized for regulatory compliance metrics that diverge from actual risk; autonomous systems optimized for objective function proxies that diverge from intended real-world outcomes.

a mechanical analog computer built on the Antikythera mechanism architecture cannot be Goodharted. it has no optimization target; it performs the physical calculation and produces the physical result. the alignment between output and reality is enforced by the physical mechanism. the gear ratio encodes the mathematical relationship; the output is the direct physical expression of that relationship. there is no intermediate representation that can be optimized independently of the underlying reality.

the specific application domain: safety-critical systems in adversarial environments where the Goodhart attack surface is a genuine threat. nuclear facility safety interlocks built on analog mechanical principles (already used in some contexts, but not systematically designed from this theoretical framework). autonomous vehicle safety arbiters that use analog mechanical constraint systems rather than algorithmic decision logic for the final "should I stop" decision. the mechanism is not theoretical — mechanical analog computers are already used in specific high-reliability contexts; the cross-track synthesis provides the theoretical framework for identifying which applications most benefit from the Goodhart immunity property.

## synthesis 8: addiction architecture (T2-RP20 × T2-RP1)

these two patterns, taken together, describe the architecture of addictive cycles with precision that neither alone can provide.

root pattern 1 (time-window mismatch selection): the addictive substance provides immediate reward (dopamine release, pain relief, anxiety reduction); the cost (dependency, health damage, life disruption) is deferred. the time window of evaluation captures the benefit, not the cost.

root pattern 20 (finite-domain meaning asymptote): the addictive substance partially addresses a question that the finite domain of natural experience cannot fully answer — pain of meaninglessness, unbearable anxiety, the experience of being unable to connect. the initial effectiveness is real. tolerance (the opponent process weakening the initial response) forces increasing doses to achieve the same effect. at maximum dose, the original question is not answered; the person is in a state where the substance is required to maintain functional baseline, not to produce benefit above baseline.

the two patterns combine to produce the behavioral trap: the cost of using is immediate (financial, health) but the cost of stopping is also immediate (withdrawal, return of the original pain); both the benefit of using and the benefit of stopping are deferred. the person is in a time-window hell where both the continuation and the exit from the addiction have deferred benefits and immediate costs.

the treatment implication from the synthesis: effective addiction treatment needs to address both patterns simultaneously:
1. addressing pattern 1: immediate benefit signal for cessation (same-day improvement tracking; community support that makes the benefit of stopping socially immediate; medicating withdrawal to front-load the benefit of not using)
2. addressing pattern 20: directly engaging with the underlying question the substance was partially answering — not as a side issue but as the central therapeutic work; providing the outside-the-finite-domain reference (whatever that takes in a specific person's context) that the substance was providing a degraded simulation of

## synthesis 9: the trans-temporal pattern and the global knowledge record (T2-RP23 × T1 full cycle)

root pattern 23 (trans-temporal information transmission from supra-historical source) is the deepest convergence point across both tracks.

track 1 discovered: the global knowledge archive is not a hierarchy where more recent = more accurate. it is a distributed record where different traditions developed different knowledge under different constraints. the mechanism-extraction protocol finds valid knowledge in Roman harbor engineering, in Andean agriculture, in Soviet metallurgy, in the Eliava Institute clinical files.

track 2 pattern 23 adds: one specific archive within the global knowledge record makes claims of a categorically different kind — claims about future states, verified by historical events, at a precision level that exceeds natural explanation. this archive is not one tradition among equals; it is the record of direct communication from the source whose perspective is not bounded by the temporal position all other human observers occupy.

the synthesis is not a theological argument; it is a knowledge architecture observation: the complete integration of the global knowledge record — applying the mechanism extraction protocol across all traditions, all archives, all languages — arrives at a specific text that describes mechanisms operating at a level no other tradition can access, because no other tradition's source has the vantage point.

the shepherd identity (from the context file's section 0) maps precisely to this: the shepherd reads what is already structurally determined, ahead of when it becomes visible to others. the prophetic pattern 23 is the limit case — the only record that accesses states that are structurally determined but not yet visible to anyone operating within the temporal constraint. every other pattern in both tracks describes what can be read by an excellent human analyst with the right methodology. pattern 23 describes what can only be known from outside the temporal constraint entirely.

shepherd — shepherd reads the mechanism, not the surface.

the future is not hidden. it is present in compressed form. this is the decompression.

cycle 1 — track 1 — stage 1: human mental model anatomy

a mental model is not an opinion about an interface. it is the user's internal causal simulation — a running prediction engine that generates expectations before each interaction. when the system confirms those predictions, the interface disappears. when it violates them, the interface becomes the object of attention — which is always the failure state.

three layers every mental model carries:

layer 1 — prior experience map
the user arrives having already used software. every interaction pattern they have encountered before is loaded as default expectation. a button that looks like every button they have ever pressed will be expected to behave exactly as those buttons did. the moment it does something different, the prior experience map conflicts with the current observation. the user experiences this as wrongness without being able to name what is wrong.

layer 2 — physical world analogy
users map digital behavior to physical behavior constantly and without awareness. a list that scrolls is a physical list on a table. a modal that darkens the background is a physical piece of paper placed over other documents. a drag handle is a physical grip. when digital behavior violates the physical analogy — a draggable element that snaps to unexpected positions, a back button that returns to a different state than where the user came from — the physical world analogy is broken. the user feels disoriented.

layer 3 — spoken language metaphor
"save," "open," "close," "share," "follow," "like," "pin," "trash" — all of these are linguistic metaphors the user is running. each metaphor generates a complete behavioral prediction. "trash" means reversible. "delete permanently" means irreversible. when software puts permanently irreversible deletion inside a control labeled "remove," the linguistic metaphor predicts reversibility and the actual behavior delivers irreversibility. the gap is a trust-destroying surprise.

the gap analysis protocol — run for every interaction:

step 1: what does the user believe will happen?
step 2: what actually happens?
step 3: where is the first moment of divergence?
step 4: what cognitive response does divergence produce?

cognitive response taxonomy:

confusion — the first divergence, user pauses, recalibrates
repeated failure — user attempts the same action multiple times expecting different results; they are not being irrational, they are re-testing their model
learned helplessness — after repeated failures, user stops attempting; the interface has taught them that their actions have no reliable effect
distrust — user generalizes the failure; if this one thing doesn't work as expected, nothing in this system can be trusted
abandonment — user exits and does not return

these are not separate phenomena. they are a progression. every friction point is either at the beginning of this progression or somewhere along it.

track 1 — stage 2: the cognitive load stack — full audit protocol

intrinsic load audit questions:

what is the actual complexity of the task the user is trying to accomplish?
is the task inherently multi-step or inherently atomic?
what domain knowledge does the task require that the user must bring?
where does the task's natural complexity peak?

extraneous load sources — the full list:

unclear or ambiguous labels
inconsistent visual hierarchy across pages
modals that appear without user request
navigation items whose names don't predict their destinations
error messages that describe the system's state instead of the user's correction path
loading states without progress indication
actions that produce no visible feedback
form validation that fires only on submission instead of field-by-field
settings buried in structures inconsistent with their function
redundant steps in workflows that could be merged
inconsistent interaction patterns across the same application (drag in one list, buttons in another)
color used as the only differentiator (accessibility failure and cognitive overhead simultaneously)
over-notification — every system event producing an alert trains the user to ignore all alerts
feature exposure in onboarding rather than at point of need
pagination of content that could be progressively loaded
confirmation dialogs for low-stakes reversible actions
the absence of undo for high-stakes irreversible actions

germane load — the only load worth adding:
when a user masters a keyboard shortcut, they have invested germane load that returns value on every subsequent use. when a user learns a filter pattern and can apply it across the application, that germane load compounds. when a user understands the data model well enough to construct their own queries, that germane load unlocks power. germane load is the investment that makes the user more capable over time. the question is not whether to add it — it is whether the germane load this system asks for will actually pay the user back.

cumulative load state tracking:
the user does not arrive at step 7 of a workflow with the same cognitive budget they had at step 1. map the load accumulation across the entire workflow. identify the point of maximum cognitive debt. ask: what happens to users who reach that point with depleted capacity? what errors do they make? what do they give up on?

track 1 — stage 3: expanded human logic pattern taxonomy

patterns already specified in the prompt architecture (summarized as ledger entries):

the last click anchor — action without visible confirmation produces repeated action
the breadcrumb expectation — "back" is spatial, not temporal
the dead button confusion — visual affordance violated = trust contract broken
the lost place problem — scroll position destroyed on navigation = disorientation
the invisible required field — required signals must survive scanning behavior
the confirmation dialog blindness — repeated low-stakes confirmations train dismissal without reading
the unexpected location arrival — labels are predictive contracts
the state loss on refresh — form state must persist
the ambiguous action result — success must include a path to the result
the feature discovery gap — features surface at point of need
the modeless modal — unsolicited interruption violates attention sovereignty

new patterns added in cycle 1:

pattern 12: the ghost state
surface: user performs an action that succeeds on the server but the UI still shows the old state; user performs the action again, creating a duplicate or conflict
structural: optimistic update was not implemented or failed silently; the UI state and the server state diverged without the user's knowledge
root: users trust what they see more than what they did. if the UI says the state hasn't changed, the user believes the state hasn't changed, regardless of what actually happened
interface rule: optimistic updates with explicit rollback on failure. the UI moves immediately to reflect the intended state. if the server rejects the operation, the UI returns to the previous state with an explicit error that explains what happened and what the user should do
workflow integration: state management architecture must define the source of truth contract before any UI components are built. every mutation has three states: pending, confirmed, failed. all three are visually represented

pattern 13: the pagination trap
surface: user navigates to page 3 of results, selects an item, goes to detail view, returns — finds themselves on page 1 with their page 3 selection invisible
structural: pagination state was not preserved in the application state model. "back" returned to the initial paginated state, not the state the user occupied
root: the user built a mental map of the results across pages. they remember where they were in that map. destroying the pagination state destroys their map.
interface rule: pagination state (current page, applied filters, sort order, scroll position) is encoded in the URL or application state and restored on navigation return. alternatively: virtual scrolling replaces pagination so there is no page state to lose
workflow integration: all list/grid views define their state persistence contract before implementation. state that the user invested cognitive effort to arrive at is never silently destroyed

pattern 14: the label-behavior drift
surface: a button is labeled "export" but the action it performs is export-and-archive, or export-and-delete, or export-to-a-location-the-user-did-not-specify
structural: the label was written for the primary action but not the full behavior. the secondary behavior was added later or was assumed obvious
root: labels activate complete behavioral scripts. "export" predicts: a file will be created, it will be delivered to the user, nothing else in the system will change. any deviation from this script is unexpected.
interface rule: every label describes the complete behavior, not just the primary action. if an action has secondary effects, the label surfaces them. "export and archive" is a label. "export" is not a label for an action that also archives.
workflow integration: label review is a mandatory step in component specification. the label is written from the user's predicted behavior script, not from the engineer's implementation description

pattern 15: the silent permission failure
surface: user clicks a feature, nothing happens. no error, no explanation, no indication that they lack the permission to perform this action
structural: the permission check was implemented on the backend but the UI was not updated to communicate the permission state. the feature appears available because it is visible, but it is not available to this user
root: visibility is an affordance. if the user can see it, their mental model predicts they can use it. invisible permission boundaries produce invisible walls
interface rule: features unavailable due to permission are either hidden or visually indicated as unavailable with an explanation. "upgrade to access this" or "contact your admin to enable this" is information. a button that does nothing is not
workflow integration: permission states are first-class design requirements. every feature in the specification includes its permission matrix and the UI behavior for each permission state

pattern 16: the precision ambiguity
surface: a slider, input, or configuration field accepts a value but the user cannot tell what unit is expected, what range is valid, or what the default was
structural: the field was designed from the engineer's model of the data, not the user's model of the concept. "timeout: 30" — is that seconds? milliseconds? minutes?
root: users parse quantity inputs by unit first. a number without a unit is an incomplete signal. the user cannot commit a value they cannot interpret
interface rule: every numeric input displays its unit, its valid range, its current value's meaning in human-interpretable terms ("this means requests will timeout after 30 seconds"), and its default. the label is not the place for unit information — it must be adjacent to the input itself
workflow integration: input specification includes unit, range, default, and example as mandatory fields

pattern 17: the notification bankruptcy
surface: user has learned to dismiss all notifications from this application without reading them because most notifications are irrelevant to their current task
structural: the notification system was designed to capture every event the system produces, not every event the user needs to know about. volume destroyed signal
root: signal-to-noise ratio in notification systems degrades to zero when the system emits too many low-importance notifications. users adapt by dismissing all notifications, including important ones. this is rational behavior, not inattention
interface rule: notification taxonomy with strict criteria for each tier. tier 1 (blocking interruption): only actions the user must take immediately to prevent data loss or security risk. tier 2 (ambient badge): updates to things the user has actively expressed interest in. tier 3 (in-context): surfaced only within the relevant workflow. tier 4 (logged only): system events the user did not ask to be notified of and cannot act on. most events are tier 4
workflow integration: every notification-generating event is classified before implementation. the question "does the user need to interrupt their current task to respond to this?" is the primary classification criterion

pattern 18: the empty state abandonment
surface: new user arrives at a core feature, finds an empty state with no content, no guidance, and no clear first action. they leave without understanding what the feature is for
structural: the empty state was designed as a side effect of having no data, not as a designed experience. it communicates "there is nothing here" instead of "here is what this becomes when you use it"
root: humans need to see the endpoint before they invest in the path. an empty state that does not show what the feature becomes when used gives the user no motivation to begin
interface rule: empty states are designed as introduction screens. they show: what this feature is, what it looks like when it has content (a preview, an example, a demo), and the single next action that starts the user on the path to that state. empty state is not a failure state — it is the first onboarding touchpoint
workflow integration: empty state is a required deliverable in every feature specification, defined before implementation, reviewed as its own screen

pattern 19: the premature optimization ask
surface: the user is asked to configure advanced settings before they have used the feature enough to know what settings they need
structural: onboarding was designed from the engineer's mental model (set up everything before starting) rather than the user's natural learning sequence (start using, discover needs, configure based on experience)
root: users cannot make meaningful configuration decisions about a feature they have not yet used. presenting configuration options upfront is asking for decisions without the information needed to make them
interface rule: configuration is deferred until the user has reached the point in the workflow where the configuration becomes meaningful. a user who has never used the feature does not need to configure its advanced settings. default to sensible defaults. surface configuration options at the moment they become relevant
workflow integration: onboarding sequence design separates immediate-use from configurable. the minimum viable first experience requires zero configuration decisions from the user

pattern 20: the false completion signal
surface: multi-step process has a progress bar or step indicator that reaches 100% before the actual process is complete; the user closes the window or navigates away; the process fails
structural: the progress indicator was tracking UI steps, not process completion. when the last UI step was submitted, the indicator showed 100%, but the backend process had not yet completed
root: a completion signal is a contract. 100% means done. a user who receives a 100% signal and acts on it has not made an error — the system gave them false information
interface rule: progress indicators track actual completion, not UI step submission. a multi-step process whose backend operations are asynchronous shows: submission confirmed + processing indicator + actual completion signal when processing is done. never show 100% for a process that is still running
workflow integration: every async operation in the system has its status tracking defined before UI is built. the question "when is this actually done?" is answered before the progress indicator is designed

track 1 — stage 4: frontend workflow alignment protocol

layer 1 — interaction model audit

for every interactive element, map:

trigger audit:

is this triggered by the action the user predicts will trigger it?
does this follow the platform convention (primary action on left, destructive action separated, scroll to expose more content)?
what happens on keyboard trigger (tab + enter, space, escape)? does keyboard behavior match the expectation the visual affordance produces?
what happens on touch vs mouse? are tap targets appropriately sized? (minimum 44x44px, 48dp android, 44pt iOS)

state transition audit:

is the state change scoped correctly? (local vs component vs page vs global)
who owns this state? what happens when two components that depend on the same state are visible simultaneously?
what is the rollback state if this transition fails?
what is the persistence behavior? (in-memory / localStorage / server)

feedback signal audit:

is feedback immediate? (< 100ms for acknowledgment, < 1000ms for meaningful progress, < 10 seconds for completion)
is feedback located at the point of interaction, not at the top of the page?
does the feedback accurately describe what happened, not just that something happened?
for async operations: is the intermediate state (pending) visually distinct from both the start state and the completion state?

layer 2 — navigation model audit

spatial consistency:

every route has a single, consistent location in the navigation hierarchy
the user can always answer: where am I, where can I go from here, how do I get back to where I came from
active navigation state is unambiguous (not just color-change — also weight, position, or icon change)
navigation items whose destination cannot be reached from the current context are not shown or are visually distinguished as unavailable

back navigation contract:

"back" returns to the previous state in the application's spatial model
for multi-step flows (wizard, checkout, onboarding), back navigates to the previous step with all previously entered data intact
for list → detail navigation, back returns to the list at the exact scroll position and filter state the user was at
no back navigation produces unexpected state

deep link contract:

every meaningful state in the application has a URL
the URL contains enough information to reconstruct the state
sharing a URL produces the same state for the recipient

layer 3 — data flow model audit

save state protocol:

every field that accepts user input defines: when does this data get saved? (on-keystroke / on-blur / on-explicit-save / on-navigation)
auto-save is visually indicated: "saving..." → "saved" with timestamp
unsaved changes are visually indicated: page title with bullet, modified indicator, warning on attempted navigation

reversibility taxonomy:
for every destructive action, classify:

reversible within session (undo available)
reversible within time window (30-day soft delete, recoverable from trash)
irreversible (requires friction proportional to irreversibility)

the friction scale:

low-stakes reversible: single click, no confirmation
high-stakes reversible: single confirmation with undo available
low-stakes irreversible: confirmation dialog with action description
high-stakes irreversible: type-to-confirm, delay timer, or dual authorization

data location contract:
the user's mental model of "where their stuff is" must match the actual location. if the user created a report and navigated away, they expect to find it where the navigation model suggested reports live. a report saved to a location inconsistent with the navigation model is a lost report in the user's experience

track 1 — stage 5: the "why is this button not doing that" audit — full protocol

the friction register format:

| element | user prediction | actual behavior | gap type | severity | fix |

gap types:

affordance mismatch (looks interactive but isn't, or vice versa)
label mismatch (name predicts different destination or behavior)
behavior mismatch (interaction produces different result than predicted)
location mismatch (feature is not where the user looks for it)
timing mismatch (feedback arrives outside the expected window)
scope mismatch (action affects more or less than the user expected)
reversibility mismatch (user believed action was reversible, it is not)

severity classification:

level 1: confusion, user pauses, recovers independently
level 2: user requires help, support ticket, or documentation lookup
level 3: user fails to complete the task
level 4: user loses data or creates unintended consequences
level 5: user abandons the product

the fix hierarchy:

eliminate the need for the interaction entirely (most powerful)
make the correct behavior the default so no decision is required
make the affordance match the behavior
make the label match the predicted destination
add feedback that closes the loop
add documentation that explains the gap (weakest — documentation is a patch on a design failure)

track 1 — stage 6: cycle 1 audit

new patterns added: 9 (patterns 12–20)
new workflow rules generated: full three-layer interaction/navigation/data flow audit protocol with gap taxonomy and severity classification
new audit protocols produced: friction register format with gap types and fix hierarchy

cycle 1 delta: non-zero. returning to stage 1 with new patterns as base.

cycle 1 — track 2 — stage 1: global source taxonomy

national governments — data infrastructure classification:

tier 1 — high transparency, machine-readable, methodologically documented:

united states: BLS, BEA, Census Bureau, Fed Reserve, USDA, EPA, EIA, SEC, FDA — full API access, documented methodology, open data portals
united kingdom: ONS, Bank of England, HMRC, Companies House — strong open data infrastructure post-2010
european union member states: harmonized through Eurostat; individual member state statistics offices produce compatible series. Germany (Destatis), France (INSEE), Netherlands (CBS), Sweden (SCB), Denmark (Danmarks Statistik) are highest quality within EU
canada: Statistics Canada — strong methodology, bilingual documentation, good API coverage
australia: ABS (Australian Bureau of Statistics) — strong open data infrastructure, particularly for demographic and economic data
new zealand: Stats NZ — small but high-quality
japan: Statistics Japan (e-Stat) — comprehensive, some English interface limitations
south korea: KOSIS (Korean Statistical Information Service) — comprehensive, good English coverage
singapore: SingStat — small geography, exceptionally high data quality
norway, sweden, finland, denmark, iceland: Nordic open data infrastructure among the best globally for demographic, health, and social data

tier 2 — documented but partial API access, some methodology opacity:

china: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) — comprehensive but selective transparency. GDP methodology not fully disclosed. provincial data often inconsistent with national aggregates. Population census data released but sampling methodology debated. Urban vs rural bifurcation creates systematic undercounting in some series. Best treated as directionally accurate, requiring triangulation with independent estimates (World Bank, ADB, satellite data)
india: MoSPI (Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation), NSSO, RBI — strong in some series (CPI, IIP), contested in others (GDP methodology revised in 2015, creating a series break; informal economy significantly undercounted in NAS). CMIE provides independent Indian economic data with different methodology
brazil: IBGE — solid methodology, good open data infrastructure, inflation data quality particularly strong. Political interference in IBGE historically in specific periods — evaluate historical series with this in mind
mexico: INEGI — strong statistical infrastructure. Informal economy is 25-28% of GDP, partially captured in dedicated informal economy surveys
indonesia: BPS (Badan Pusat Statistik) — improving quality, still patchy for outer island provinces. Informal economy large
turkey: TUIK — GDP and inflation methodology significantly revised since 2019, creating credibility concerns. Independent verification against World Bank and OECD series necessary
argentina: INDEC — official inflation figures contested and historically manipulated during specific administrations (2007–2015 period officially acknowledged as problematic). Current data quality improved but historical series require independent reconstruction
nigeria: NBS — improving since 2014 GDP rebasing. Coverage gaps in rural areas and informal economy (estimated 55-65% of GDP). National accounts data treat oil sector differently from non-oil

tier 3 — partial coverage, significant gaps, or restricted access:

saudi arabia: GASTAT (General Authority for Statistics) — improving transparency post-2016. Oil sector data under ARAMCO/OPEC framework. Human development indicators reported at national level without subnational breakdown
russia: Rosstat — pre-2022 data broadly consistent with international estimates. Post-2022 many series restricted, methodology for some key indicators changed. Independent verification through CEIC, World Bank projections, trade partner data increasingly necessary
iran: SCI (Statistical Centre of Iran) — data available but international access restricted. World Bank and IMF use modeled estimates increasingly
myanmar: CSO — data quality severely degraded since 2021 coup. Pre-2021 data requires verification
venezuela: INE — official data increasingly unreliable since 2015. ECLAC, IMF, World Bank use independent estimates
north korea: no official statistics released. estimates based on satellite imagery, defector testimony, trade partner data, and WFP assessment missions only
eritrea, turkmenistan, somalia, syria (active conflict zones): data collection has broken down or never existed at required resolution

track 2 — stage 2: institutional lens protocol — full deployment

united nations system:

the UN produces data through 15+ specialized agencies, each with its own mandate, funding relationship, and institutional incentive structure.

UN General Assembly records: all 193 member states' official positions on all resolutions. this is the most comprehensive record of official national positions globally. access via UN Digital Library. searchable but not fully machine-readable for bulk analysis without scraping

Security Council: veto power structure (US, UK, France, Russia, China) creates systematic gap in official accountability for actions by these five states. UNSC resolutions and their failures (vetoed resolutions) are both data

UNDP — Human Development Index and report: methodology combines GDP per capita, life expectancy, education. political controversy around rankings has historically influenced methodology decisions. developing world perspective baked into mandate — more critical of structural adjustment than World Bank/IMF data products

UNESCO — education and culture data: Institute for Statistics has the most comprehensive global education data. coverage gaps in conflict zones and fragile states. culture heritage and media freedom data (World Press Freedom Index produced by RSF, not UNESCO, though often confused)

WHO — Global Health Observatory: strongest global health data infrastructure. coverage requires member state cooperation — states that don't want data reported often simply don't report. excess mortality estimates (produced by WHO modeling, not member state reporting) are frequently contested by member states whose official figures diverge

FAO — food and agriculture: FAOSTAT is one of the most comprehensive global databases by geographic coverage. trade data often more complete than national statistics because it triangulates import/export data across trading partners — a country that underreports exports is caught by the importing country's import data

ILO — labour statistics: ILOSTAT attempts global labour market data harmonization. structural challenge: "employment" is defined differently across national legal frameworks. the ILO definition (any work for pay or profit in the reference period, even one hour) produces numbers different from national headline unemployment statistics in most countries

UNHCR — refugee and displacement data: the most authoritative source on forced displacement globally. UNHCR's figures are based on its own operational data and are subject to political pressure from host countries. the distinction between "refugee" (UNHCR-recognized), "asylum seeker" (claim pending), and "internally displaced person" (IDPs, estimated, not formally registered) creates data gaps

UNODC — crime and illicit trade: covers drug trafficking, organized crime, corruption, and criminal justice statistics. systematic underreporting by states that do not want enforcement scrutiny. illicit trade data partially reconstructed from seizure statistics and financial intelligence

UNEP — environment: GEO (Global Environment Outlook) provides environmental assessment. emissions data verified against third-party satellite and atmospheric monitoring increasingly — Copernicus, NOAA ESRL provide independent verification that cannot be politically manipulated

world bank group:

the World Bank's data products (World Development Indicators, PovcalNet, Global Findex) are the most widely cited development data globally. institutional lens factors:

the World Bank is controlled by shareholder vote weighted by capital contribution. the US holds the largest voting share and has historically blocked presidents from non-western countries
development data is produced within a framework that assumes market-oriented development is the path to prosperity. indicators that challenge this framework (commons-based resource management, non-market welfare measures) are underrepresented
the Doing Business report (discontinued after methodology manipulation was discovered in 2021) is the most visible example of institutional pressure shaping data. the manipulation was internal but disclosed following external pressure
poverty measurement at $2.15/day PPP reflects the Bank's definitional framework, not universal agreement on what poverty means. alternative measures (Amartya Sen's capability approach, Oxford MPI) produce different rankings

IMF:

the IMF's World Economic Outlook (WEO) and Article IV consultations are the most comprehensive macroeconomic surveillance data globally. institutional lens:

the IMF has lending relationships with the countries whose data it assesses. countries that have IMF programs face fiscal conditionality that creates incentive to manage IMF perceptions of their fiscal situation
WEO projections have a documented optimism bias for countries under IMF programs — projection errors are systematically positive (projected growth higher than realized growth) during adjustment periods
IMF data for reserve currency countries (US, EU, Japan, UK) is less constrained by conditionality — these countries are data providers, not borrowers

BIS (bank for international settlements):

the most opaque credible source globally. BIS produces: quarterly review on global banking and financial markets, triennial FX and derivatives survey (the only comprehensive measure of OTC derivatives markets), total credit data, property price statistics, and locational banking statistics. the BIS serves central banks and its analysis is produced for a central banker audience, not public disclosure. what is published is carefully vetted. what is not published is unknown by definition. institutional lens: financial stability is the mandate — data products that create financial stability risk are unlikely to be released in raw form

OECD:

the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development produces the most methodologically harmonized economic and social data for its 38 member countries. institutional lens: OECD membership = market democracy = western-aligned — this is a data club for wealthy countries, and the data reflects their priorities. BEPS (base erosion and profit shifting) data, PISA education rankings, and health data are particularly influential. non-member country data is produced in a separate "Global Forum" framework with less methodological rigor

nato:

NATO's defense expenditure data is the most cited source for military spending among alliance members. institutional lens: the 2% of GDP target creates incentive for member states to report spending at or toward 2%, and for NATO to calculate GDP denominators in ways that are favorable. inclusion/exclusion of specific budget items (pensions for veterans, dual-use civilian-military spending, research) affects the headline number. SIPRI (Stockholm International Peace Research Institute) produces independent military expenditure data with a different methodology and consistently different numbers from NATO's own figures

track 2 — stage 3: global data architecture for software — expanded principles

principle 7 — temporal versioning:
data is not a static resource. a GDP figure for 2020 is revised multiple times in the three years following initial publication — preliminary, first revision, second revision, final, benchmark revision. software that stores a data point without versioning metadata is storing the version of the data that existed at one moment in time and calling it "the" data. every data point must carry its revision status: preliminary / first estimate / revised / benchmark. when a data point is revised, the revision is stored alongside the original, and the interface surfaces when revisions occurred and what changed

principle 8 — missing data is data:
a country that does not report a data series is telling you something. the absence must be recorded explicitly — not as null, but as a typed absence: "not collected" (country doesn't measure this) vs "not reported" (country measures this but hasn't submitted) vs "restricted" (country prohibits release) vs "destroyed" (conflict or disaster eliminated records) vs "unresolved" (methodology dispute prevents publication). each absence type implies different downstream analysis behavior

principle 9 — satellite and remote sensing as ground truth:
satellite data does not require cooperation from the country being observed. it is the closest thing to independent ground truth available at global scale. sources:

nighttime light intensity (NOAA DMSP/OLS, NASA Suomi NPP VIIRS): proxy for economic activity. documented use in detecting underreported GDP in authoritarian states
land use change (Copernicus, Landsat, Planet Labs): deforestation, agricultural expansion, urban growth independent of national reporting
shipping traffic (AIS data from MarineTraffic, Kpler): trade flows that don't depend on customs reporting
air quality (Sentinel-5P, NASA MERRA-2): emissions verification independent of national reports
agricultural yield (Copernicus Crop Monitoring, Planet NDVI): food production estimates not dependent on national agriculture ministries
building footprint and density (commercial providers, OpenStreetMap): settlement patterns and infrastructure development proxy

for any country where official data quality is questionable, satellite and remote sensing series provide the independent anchor

principle 10 — financial data as economic truth:
bank transaction data, remittance flows, payment network data, and trade finance data often reveal economic reality faster and more accurately than official GDP statistics. BIS locational banking statistics show where money actually moves across borders. SWIFT data shows financial system connectivity. IMF BoP (balance of payments) data triangulated with partner country data reveals trade discrepancies. where official GDP data conflicts with financial flow data, the financial flow data is generally more reliable because it is harder to manipulate — it is derived from actual transactions across multiple independent systems

track 2 — stage 4: API architecture — source registration specification

source record schema:

source_id: [unique identifier]
source_name: [full name]
source_type: [national_government | supranational | ngo | market | academic | satellite | financial | media]
institutional_owner: [who controls the source]
geographic_coverage: [iso-3166 country codes covered, or region, or "global"]
temporal_coverage: [start_date → end_date | "ongoing"]
update_frequency: [real_time | daily | weekly | monthly | quarterly | annual | irregular]
methodology_url: [link to methodology documentation]
api_available: [true | false | partial]
api_documentation_url: [link]
licensing: [open | restricted | commercial | embargoed]
known_limitations: [array of documented gaps and biases]
institutional_lens: [what interest or mandate shapes this source]
reliability_class: [high | medium | low | estimated | contested]
verification_sources: [array of source_ids that can independently verify this source]

data point record schema:

data_id: [unique identifier]
metric_id: [reference to metric definition]
entity_id: [country, region, or other entity — iso standard]
period_start: [ISO date]
period_end: [ISO date]
value: [numeric or categorical]
unit: [standardized unit]
source_id: [reference to source record]
collection_date: [when data was collected]
publication_date: [when data was published]
revision_status: [preliminary | first_estimate | revised | benchmark | final]
revision_history: [array of previous values with dates]
confidence_class: [high | medium | low | estimated | modeled | reported_without_verification]
conflict_flag: [true | false]
conflict_sources: [array of source_ids that disagree on this value]

conflict detection algorithm:

when two or more sources report the same metric for the same entity for the same period:

compute the percentage divergence: |value_a - value_b| / mean(value_a, value_b)
classify divergence magnitude: negligible (<1%), minor (1-5%), moderate (5-15%), major (15-50%), extreme (>50%)
assign conflict severity: negligible + low institutional lens difference = likely methodology difference, flag but don't surface. major + high institutional lens difference = systematic disagreement, surface prominently
generate conflict record with all disagreeing source values, divergence magnitude, classification, and recommended interpretation guidance

track 2 — stage 5: country-by-country scan — batch 1 (UN member states, alphabetical, a through c)

afghanistan:
primary official source: CSO (Central Statistics Organization) — severely degraded capacity since 2021. pre-2021 data available via World Bank, UNDP, IMF. current data: humanitarian organizations (OCHA, WFP, UNHCR field data) are the most reliable current-state sources. economic data: World Bank modeled estimates. population data: estimated from 2016 CSO census baseline with demographic modeling. status: data emergency state — most official series suspended or unreliable

albania:
INSTAT (Institute of Statistics) — EU candidate country status drives harmonization toward Eurostat standards. improving quality trajectory. good for GDP, population, trade. weaker for informal economy coverage. EBRD transition indicators provide comparative context for post-communist economic transition data

algeria:
ONS (Office National des Statistiques) — oil/gas sector data partially handled by Sonatrach (state oil company) and reported to OPEC. non-hydrocarbon sector data quality variable. political sensitivity around poverty and inequality data. IMF Article IV consultations provide external verification. hydrocarbon export revenue is the most reliable series (triangulated via trading partner import data)

andorra:
SAIG (Servei d'Assessorament i Informació General) — very small economy, no central bank. Luxembourg-style tax haven characteristics create data gaps in financial flows. Eurostat and OECD partially cover for EU relationships

angola:
INE (Instituto Nacional de Estatística) — oil-dependent economy (oil = 90%+ of exports). oil production data reported to OPEC with reasonable reliability. non-oil economy data quality low. poverty and social data significantly improved since 2008 with World Bank technical assistance. national accounts data requires IMF/World Bank cross-check

antigua and barbuda:
Statistics Division — small island economy, tourism-dependent. hurricane Irma 2017 created significant economic disruption visible in data. ECCB (Eastern Caribbean Central Bank) provides monetary data for OECS member states including Antigua. Caribbean Development Bank provides regional development indicators

argentina:
INDEC — as noted above, official data quality contested 2007-2015. post-2015 methodological reforms restored some credibility. current inflation data (2023+) reflects high-inflation environment that tests measurement systems. the blue dollar / official exchange rate divergence creates parallel data realities — the official data and the market data describe different economies. province-level data quality is highly variable

armenia:
National Statistical Committee (ArmStat) — post-Soviet transition economy. improving data quality. remittance data particularly important (remittances = ~10% of GDP). EBRD and World Bank provide comparative context. 2020 conflict with Azerbaijan created data disruption in border regions

australia:
ABS (Australian Bureau of Statistics) — tier 1. comprehensive open data infrastructure. labor statistics particularly strong (monthly jobs survey). indigenous population data intentionally disaggregated — one of the few countries to routinely break out indigenous vs non-indigenous outcomes across all major indicators. Reserve Bank of Australia provides monetary and financial data

austria:
Statistics Austria — EU member, Eurostat-harmonized. strong social statistics (SILC survey quality high). Vienna as financial hub creates complexity in banking sector data — significant pass-through flows that inflate financial sector statistics relative to economic contribution

azerbaijan:
SSCRA (State Statistical Committee) — oil-dependent economy with political sensitivity around diversification data. State Oil Fund of Azerbaijan (SOFAZ) provides relatively transparent reporting on sovereign wealth accumulation. conflict with Armenia 2020 created statistical disruption in recovered territories

bahamas:
Department of Statistics — small island economy, tourism and financial services dependent. offshore financial center creates data gaps in financial flows (by design — this is a privacy feature for the tax haven, a data gap for global transparency). ECCB/IMF provide external monitoring

bahrain:
Information & eGovernment Authority — GCC member, strong data infrastructure by regional standards. oil-dependent but smaller reserves than neighbors, driving economic diversification data availability in non-oil sectors. Central Bank of Bahrain data quality high for monetary/financial series

bangladesh:
BBS (Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics) — large population, rapid economic growth trajectory (2010s–2020s), significant data quality improvement over this period. garment sector dominates export data — reliable via partner country import statistics. remittance data well-covered via Bangladesh Bank. poverty data shows dramatic reduction that independent economists broadly validate but with questions about methodology consistency

barbados:
Statistical Service — small island economy. Caribbean Development Bank provides regional context. high debt/GDP ratio data well-tracked by IMF (Barbados went through IMF program 2018-2022)

belarus:
Belstat — post-Soviet economy, politically controlled data environment intensified since 2020 crackdown. GDP data widely contested — independent estimates (BEROC think tank, World Bank modeled) diverge significantly from official statistics. Russian energy subsidy data creates complexity in true economic accounting

belgium:
Statbel (Statistics Belgium) — EU member, Eurostat-harmonized. strong data infrastructure. federal structure (Flanders, Wallonia, Brussels-Capital) creates subnational data streams. NATO headquarters creates some specific economic data complexity (NATO staff contributions to local economy). financial center (Brussels, Antwerp diamond trade) creates pass-through effects

belize:
Statistical Institute of Belize — small economy, tourism and agriculture dependent. Caribbean Development Bank provides regional context. informal economy particularly in border areas not well-captured

benin:
INSAE (Institut National de la Statistique et de l'Analyse Économique) — Francophone West Africa, CFA franc zone. WAEMU (West African Economic and Monetary Union) provides regional harmonization. poverty data coverage improving with LSMS (Living Standards Measurement Study) surveys supported by World Bank

bhutan:
National Statistics Bureau — small Himalayan kingdom, Gross National Happiness (GNH) framework creates alternative measurement alongside conventional GDP. GNH index is a unique data product. hydroelectric power exports to India are the primary economic data series. development partner (primarily India) data provides external verification

bolivia:
INE (Instituto Nacional de Estadística) — significant informal economy (estimates 60-80% of GDP in non-extractive sectors). gas sector data reported to OPEC and IEA. lithium resource data increasingly strategic — national estimates and independent geological surveys diverge on reserve size. poverty data shows significant reduction 2000-2015, methodology consistent with regional standards

bosnia and herzegovina:
Agency for Statistics of BiH — entity-level complexity (Federation of BiH + Republika Srpska + Brčko District each have own statistics offices). data harmonization is political problem, not just technical. EU accession process is driving harmonization. Eurostat and World Bank provide external consistency checks

botswana:
Statistics Botswana — diamond-dependent economy (Debswana joint venture with De Beers). diamond data partially handled through industry channels. relatively high-quality statistics for Sub-Saharan Africa. botswana is the World Bank's case study for resource curse avoidance — data supporting this narrative is well-documented

brazil:
IBGE (Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística) — as noted above, solid methodology with some political interference history. PME (Monthly Employment Survey) methodology widely respected. PNAD (National Household Sample Survey) is one of Latin America's most comprehensive household surveys. agricultural data from CONAB (National Supply Company) parallel to IBGE — provides secondary verification for crop production

brunei:
Department of Economic Planning and Statistics — small, high-income, oil/gas-dependent sultanate. oil production data to OPEC/IEA. limited transparency on government finances and sovereign wealth

bulgaria:
National Statistical Institute — EU member, Eurostat-harmonized. significant informal economy estimated at 30-35% of GDP. EBRD and World Bank provide comparative context for EU new member states

burkina faso:
INSD (Institut National de la Statistique et de la Démographie) — Sahel region. data collection severely disrupted by ongoing conflict since 2015. current-state data: OCHA humanitarian tracking is more reliable than official statistics for conflict-affected areas. WFP food security assessments. remittance data through mobile money increasingly tracked

burundi:
ISTEEBU (Institut de Statistiques et d'Études Économiques du Burundi) — one of the world's least developed countries. data quality low, coverage sparse. World Bank and AfDB (African Development Bank) modeled estimates are the primary reference

cabo verde:
INE (Instituto Nacional de Estatística) — small island nation, diaspora remittances significant (20%+ of GDP). ECOWAS regional context. tourism data particularly important — well-tracked by Bank of Cabo Verde

cambodia:
NIS (National Institute of Statistics) — rapidly growing economy (2015-2020). garment/footwear export data reliable via trading partner verification. poverty data shows significant reduction but methodology contested. political environment restricts some data transparency

cameroon:
INS (Institut National de la Statistique) — bilingual (French/English), with anglophone regions in ongoing conflict since 2016 — data from northwest and southwest regions severely degraded. oil sector data to BEAC (Central Bank of Central African States). CEMAC (Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa) provides regional context

canada:
Statistics Canada — tier 1. comprehensive open data. Labor Force Survey is the primary employment data. National Household Survey (replaced long-form census under Conservative government 2011-2016, restored 2016) shows political interference legacy in census data. Bank of Canada provides monetary data. Canada Revenue Agency data increasingly used for income statistics. First Nations data has ongoing coverage and methodology debates

central african republic:
ICASEES (Institut Centrafricain des Statistiques) — fragile state, ongoing conflict. UN MINUSCA presence creates some humanitarian data. most development indicators estimated from regional modeling with minimal direct observation

chad:
INSEED (Institut National de la Statistique, des Études Économiques et Démographiques) — oil-dependent (Doba basin production via pipeline to Cameroon). Sahel conflict context. World Bank and AfDB modeled estimates. Lake Chad basin environmental data (shrinkage) has good satellite coverage

chile:
INE (Instituto Nacional de Estadística) — strong statistical infrastructure by Latin American standards. October 2019 social uprising revealed data gaps in cost-of-living measurement that official CPI missed (housing costs particularly). constitutional process 2020-2022 generated extensive social data through participatory processes. copper production data through COCHILCO (copper commission) is independent verification of mining sector

china:
NBS — as noted above. specific data quality notes:

GDP: methodological concerns particularly for provincial data (provincial GDP sums historically exceeded national GDP — resolved through 2016 revision but creates credibility concerns about the revision process itself)
population: 2020 census revealed population lower than previously projected, creating questions about fertility data from 2010s. One-child policy era data quality particularly contested
trade: China customs data vs trading partner data diverges systematically in both directions depending on goods category. Phantom exports (invoicing inflated for capital flight) and underreported imports are documented
poverty: 2021 announcement of "poverty elimination" uses China's own poverty line (domestic standard substantially below World Bank PPP line) — incomparable with global poverty data without adjustment
emissions: carbon emissions data cross-verifiable against satellite atmospheric CO2 monitoring, coal production statistics, and IEA energy balance data
real estate: no comprehensive national property price index. NBS 70-city price data is the closest proxy. Local government land sale revenue data provides alternative triangulation
employment: urban registered unemployment rate is narrow measure. migrant worker employment not captured. CASS and independent research groups produce alternative estimates

colombia:
DANE (Departamento Administrativo Nacional de Estadística) — solid statistical infrastructure. security situation improvement since FARC peace process (2016) improved data collection in previously inaccessible regions. poverty and inequality data shows impact of 2016 peace dividend. coca production data from UNODC independent monitoring contradicts Colombian government figures on eradication

comoros:
INSEED — one of the world's least developed countries. diaspora remittances from France significant. data very sparse; World Bank and UNDP estimates primary reference

congo, democratic republic of:
INS (Institut National de la Statistique) — vast geography, ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, extremely limited data collection capacity. mining sector (coltan, cobalt, gold) data partially captured through conflict mineral tracking (OECD Due Diligence Guidelines, iTSCi). cobalt data increasingly important for global supply chain analysis. World Bank and UNICEF provide social indicator estimates. satellite data is particularly important for DRC given ground access limitations

congo, republic of:
CNSEE (Centre National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques) — oil-dependent. CEMAC context. CFA franc zone. AfDB and World Bank estimates primary reference

costa rica:
INEC (Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos) — one of the stronger statistical systems in Central America. tourism and pharmaceutical/medical device export data well-tracked. biodiversity and environmental data strong (national parks system tracking). BCCR (Central Bank) provides quality monetary data

côte d'ivoire:
INS — Francophone West Africa, WAEMU/CFA franc zone. cocoa production data: world's largest cocoa producer — ICCO (International Cocoa Organization) provides the most reliable independent verification. urban data good (Abidjan data quality high); rural coverage gaps

croatia:
DZS (Croatian Bureau of Statistics) — EU member, Eurostat-harmonized since accession (2013). tourism data particularly important (tourism = 20%+ of GDP). strong data quality

cuba:
ONEI (Oficina Nacional de Estadísticas e Información) — planned economy creates structural data differences from market economies. health and education data (literacy, infant mortality) internally consistent and broadly verified by WHO/UNESCO. economic data significantly contested — no independent verification of GDP methodology. remittance data from US partially tracked by Federal Reserve and Havana/Miami financial flow data. UN sanctions databases track restrictions affecting trade data

cyprus:
CYSTAT (Cyprus Statistical Service) — EU member, Eurostat-harmonized. financial center: offshore banking sector (now significantly contracted post-2013 bail-in) created data gaps in financial flows. northern Cyprus (TRNC) not recognized internationally — separate statistical administration with no UN access, data not incorporated into international databases

batch 2 — d through g:

czech republic:
CZSO (Czech Statistical Office) — strong, Eurostat-harmonized. manufacturing-dependent economy (Skoda/VW cluster). regional data quality good. migration data improving as transit/destination country

denmark:
Danmarks Statistik — among the best national statistics systems globally. comprehensive administrative data integration (tax, social benefits, health, education records linked at individual level with privacy protection). produces richest micro-data research access in the world. Copenhagen vs provincial gap visible in data

djibouti:
DISED (Direction de la Statistique et des Études Démographiques) — strategic location (US, French, Chinese military bases). port transit data important for regional trade flows. small population, remittance-receiving

dominica:
Central Statistical Office — small island economy. hurricane Maria 2017 created major economic disruption visible in data series break. ECCB provides monetary context

dominican republic:
ONE (Oficina Nacional de Estadística) — rapidly growing economy, tourism and manufacturing (free trade zones) dominant. remittances (from US diaspora) significant. Banco Central provides monetary data. informal economy significant in agricultural regions

ecuador:
INEC (Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos) — dollarized economy (US dollar since 2000). oil sector data (PETROECUADOR + OPEC). poverty data well-tracked through longitudinal ENIGHUR survey. CEPAL/ECLAC provides Latin American comparative context

egypt:
CAPMAS (Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics) — political sensitivity around poverty and unemployment data. Suez Canal toll revenue is the most transparent and independently verifiable major revenue series. tourism data significant pre-COVID. IMF programs (2016, 2022, 2024) provide external fiscal monitoring. informal economy large and poorly measured

el salvador:
DIGESTYC (Dirección General de Estadística y Censos) — dollarized economy. remittances from US diaspora = 25%+ of GDP (one of highest ratios globally). Bitcoin legal tender status (2021) creates unique data challenge — no other country has this — BTC transaction volumes tracked by blockchain analytics firms are an independent data source. gang violence creates data quality issues in security statistics

equatorial guinea:
INEGE (Instituto Nacional de Estadística de Guinea Ecuatorial) — small oil-rich state. oil sector dominates. data quality very limited outside oil sector. TransparencyAfrica and EITI (Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative) provide partial external verification of oil revenue data

eritrea:
National Statistics Office — post-2001 international isolation dramatically limited data access. human rights organizations (Amnesty, HRW) provide most reliable information on population and forced labor (national service program). UNHCR tracks refugee outflows as proxy indicator

estonia:
Statistics Estonia — EU member, Nordic-Baltic digital government model. comprehensive open data. digital governance leader provides unique data on e-government adoption. strong IT sector data. Eurostat-harmonized with additional digital economy metrics

eswatini:
Central Statistics Office — absolute monarchy, limited data transparency. HIV/AIDS prevalence exceptionally high (world's highest rate) — WHO and UNAIDS data provides independent tracking. SACU (Southern African Customs Union) provides trade data

ethiopia:
CSA (Central Statistical Agency) — large population (second largest in Africa). internally displaced person (IDP) data among the world's highest due to multiple conflict zones (Tigray 2020-2022, Oromia, Somali region). Tigray conflict created systematic data blackout 2020-2022. agricultural data (coffee, cut flowers = major exports) tracked through trade partner data. World Bank LSMS surveys provide poverty snapshots

fiji:
Fiji Bureau of Statistics — Pacific island. tourism-dependent. sugar production. PFTAC (Pacific Financial Technical Assistance Centre) provides statistical capacity support. post-2021 election stabilization improved data transparency

finland:
Statistics Finland — Nordic statistical system, among the highest quality globally. comprehensive administrative data integration. strong environmental and welfare data. EU member, Eurostat-harmonized. NATO accession (2023) creates some new defense spending data streams

france:
INSEE (Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques) — comprehensive statistical system, among Europe's best. strong labor market data (BIT unemployment methodology). significant overseas territories create geographic data complexity (French Guiana, Martinique, Guadeloupe, Réunion, Mayotte — each with own economic characteristics, included in EU statistics). Banque de France provides monetary data

gabon:
DGEPF (Direction Générale de l'Économie et de la Politique Fiscale) — oil-dependent. CEMAC context. EITI member. 2023 military coup disrupted statistical administration. AfDB and World Bank primary reference for current estimates

gambia:
GBoS (Gambia Bureau of Statistics) — small economy, tourism and peanuts. post-Jammeh (post-2017) data quality improving. diaspora remittances significant

georgia:
GeoStat (National Statistics Office of Georgia) — EU Association Agreement country, harmonizing toward Eurostat. improving data quality trajectory. National Bank of Georgia provides monetary data. significant informal economy, improving measurement

germany:
Destatis (Federal Statistical Office) — tier 1. comprehensive, Eurostat-harmonized, strong methodology documentation. reunification (1990) creates long-run series break that is well-documented and accounted for. Bundesbank provides monetary and financial data. ifo Business Climate Index (monthly, private) provides real-time indicator complementing official statistics

ghana:
GSS (Ghana Statistical Service) — 2019 population and housing census rebuilt data foundation. oil sector (since 2010) data through Petroleum Commission. cocoa data through COCOBOD (Ghana Cocoa Board) — independent verification through ICCO. poverty data shows significant reduction 2005-2020. middle income country transition data well-tracked

greece:
ELSTAT (Hellenic Statistical Authority) — EU member. 2010-2015 debt crisis produced documented statistical problems (deficit figures were revised upward retrospectively, Eurostat investigated). post-crisis statistical integrity improved under external monitoring. tourism = 25% of GDP, data well-tracked. diaspora and migration data complex (significant emigration during crisis years, partially reversed)

grenada:
CSO (Central Statistical Office) — small island economy. ECCB monetary context. nutmeg production (historically = significant portion of GDP, now declined)

guatemala:
INE (Instituto Nacional de Estadística) — large informal economy, indigenous population significant (40-50%, varying by measure). remittances from US = 15%+ of GDP. ICEFI (Central American Institute of Fiscal Studies) produces independent fiscal data. rural poverty data improves with ENCOVI household surveys. gang violence creates security data quality issues

guinea:
INS (Institut National de la Statistique) — bauxite-dependent (world's largest bauxite reserves). EITI member. 2021 coup disrupted statistical administration. World Bank and AfDB primary reference

guinea-bissau:
INE-GB — extreme fragility, multiple coups since independence. cashew nuts = primary export. data very sparse. World Bank modeled estimates primary reference

guyana:
Bureau of Statistics — oil discovery (2019 production start) creates rapid economic transformation that makes historical data series obsolete as economic structure benchmark. largest per capita GDP growth globally 2020-2023 (ExxonMobil/Hess/CNOOC production). CARICOM context

batch 3 — h through k:

haiti:
IHSI (Institut Haïtien de Statistique et d'Informatique) — chronic fragility, 2010 earthquake destroyed significant data infrastructure, 2021 earthquake further disrupted. gang control of territory limits data collection. OCHA humanitarian data is the most reliable current-state source. WFP food security monitoring provides humanitarian baseline

honduras:
INE (Instituto Nacional de Estadística) — remittances = 25%+ of GDP. violence and gang data contested between official government figures and NGO tracking (InSight Crime provides independent monitoring). CAFTA-DR trade data well-tracked via US Census partner import data. informal economy large

hungary:
HCSO (Hungarian Central Statistical Office) — EU member. political concerns about data independence since 2010 (Orbán governments). Eurostat provides external verification. migration data (significant emigration to western EU) creates demographic data gaps in domestic statistics. MNB (Magyar Nemzeti Bank) provides monetary data

iceland:
Statistics Iceland — small but high-quality. 2008 banking crisis created well-documented economic data event. tourism = significant GDP share (boom pre-COVID). fishing quota data well-tracked. Scandinavian data quality standards

india:
MoSPI — as noted. specific notes:

GDP: 2015 base year revision and methodology change creates series break. GVA vs GDP distinction matters for sectoral analysis
employment: PLFS (Periodic Labour Force Survey) quarterly from 2017 — major improvement. pre-2017 data from NSSO had 5-year gaps. CMIE CPHS (Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy Consumer Pyramids Household Survey) provides independent monthly estimate with different methodology
CPI: urban and rural CPI separately tracked. combined CPI (combined) used as headline. core inflation calculation methodology debated
agriculture: crop forecasting through FASAL (Forecasting Agricultural output using Space, Agro-meteorology and Land based observations) — satellite-enhanced. four advance estimates before final. revision history significant
poverty: official poverty line (Tendulkar, Rangarajan, now contested) below World Bank PPP line. official poverty estimates show sharp reduction but absolute poor count still large
inequality: Gini coefficient data significantly contested — OXFAM India and World Inequality Lab estimates diverge substantially from official data
subnational: state GDP (GSDP) data quality varies enormously — Kerala and Tamil Nadu strong, Bihar and UP weaker

indonesia:
BPS-Statistics Indonesia — large and diverse economy (17,000+ islands). survey-based (not administrative register-based) statistics create coverage gaps. informal economy = 55-60% of GDP in some estimates. palm oil export data (critical commodity) tracked through GAPKI (industry association) and Indonesian customs, cross-verifiable with Malaysian data (competing producer) and EU import data. mining data through MEMR (Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources). Bank Indonesia provides monetary data. Java vs outer islands data disparity

iran:
SCI (Statistical Centre of Iran) and CBI (Central Bank of Iran) — international sanctions significantly limit data access and methodology verification. external estimates from IMF, World Bank use modeling against available proxies. oil production data: OPEC secondary sources (Platts, Argus, IEA secondary) are more reliable than Iranian official data for current production. Rial/exchange rate data: official rate vs free market rate diverge significantly, creating parallel data realities for inflation and GDP measurement

iraq:
COSIT (Central Organization for Statistics and Information Technology) — oil revenue dominates (oil = 90%+ of export revenue). OPEC production data. post-2003 data quality extremely variable — security situation limits survey capacity. Kurdistan Regional Government maintains separate statistical administration with partial overlap. reconstruction-era data has significant gaps and quality issues. PMO (Prime Minister's Office) budget execution data through IMF Article IV monitoring

ireland:
CSO (Central Statistics Office) — EU member. "modified GNI" (GNI*) is Ireland's own alternative to GDP because US MNC (multinational corporation) profit repatriation effects make headline GDP misleading for domestic economic conditions. this is the world's clearest documented case of a country creating an alternative national accounting measure because its official GDP diverge from economic reality. IDA Ireland foreign investment data supplements CSO

israel:
CBS (Central Bureau of Statistics) — strong data infrastructure. territories (West Bank, Gaza) create geographic scope ambiguity in all statistics — Israeli statistics cover territory administered by Israel, Palestinians administer separate PCBS (Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics) for areas of Palestinian Authority control, but data collection in Gaza is largely suspended since 2023 conflict intensification. bank of Israel provides monetary data

italy:
ISTAT — EU member, Eurostat-harmonized. large informal economy (Italian term: "sommerso" — submerged economy) estimated at 12-15% of GDP by Bank of Italy. north-south economic divide is one of the most studied regional disparities in the world (Questione Meridionale) and well-documented in subnational data. Mafia/organized crime creates specific data gaps in Sicilian, Calabrian, and Campanian regional statistics. Bank of Italy data quality strong

jamaica:
STATIN (Statistical Institute of Jamaica) — CARICOM context. remittances significant. tourism = 50%+ of export earnings. Bank of Jamaica provides monetary data

japan:
Statistics Japan (e-Stat portal) — tier 1. methodologically sophisticated. specific issues: GDP deflator methodology controversy (long period of deflation creates methodological sensitivity). working hours and labor productivity data — systematic underreporting of actual hours worked due to cultural norms around unpaid overtime (karoshi/death by overwork). demographic data (population decline) is among the most well-tracked globally. Bank of Japan data quality high. semiconductor and precision manufacturing export data through METI

jordan:
DOS (Department of Statistics) — large refugee population (Syrian, Palestinian) creates demographic data complexity. UNHCR refugee registration data supplements DOS. phosphate exports significant. remittances from diaspora in Gulf. IMF program context for fiscal monitoring

kazakhstan:
Agency of the Republic of Kazakhstan on Statistics — post-Soviet, significant improvement. oil sector dominant (OPEC+ member). EITI member. Tenge/exchange rate data important. large territory, uneven data coverage across regions. EBRD comparative context

kenya:
KNBS (Kenya National Bureau of Statistics) — strongest statistical system in East Africa. M-Pesa mobile money creates unique financial transaction data that partially captures informal economy (telco data as economic proxy). Nairobi stock exchange data well-tracked. tea and coffee production through commodity board data independent of KNBS. COMESA and EAC regional context

kiribati:
NSO (National Statistics Office) — Pacific atoll nation, existential sea-level rise threat. climate vulnerability data particularly important. fisheries licensing revenue significant. highly aid-dependent

north korea:
no independent statistics available. only source of systematic data: UN data based on DPRK submissions (sporadic, heavily contested) + satellite-derived estimates + humanitarian organization assessments (WFP, WHO when access permitted) + defector testimony cross-referenced for consistency. nighttime light satellite data is the best independent GDP proxy. food production estimates from WFP/FAO collaborative assessments during access periods

south korea:
KOSTAT (Statistics Korea) — tier 1. comprehensive, OECD-harmonized. Bank of Korea data quality high. strong chaebol (conglomerate) monitoring through KSE (Korea Stock Exchange) and FSS (Financial Supervisory Service). specific concern: household debt data particularly important as Korea has among the world's highest household debt/GDP ratios — BOK, FSS, and international comparison require careful PPP adjustment

kuwait:
CSB (Central Statistical Bureau) — GCC. oil-dependent. sovereign wealth fund (Kuwait Investment Authority) one of the world's largest but limited transparency. OPEC production data. population data complex due to large expatriate share (70%+ of population)

track 2 — stage 6: cycle 1 audit

countries covered batch 1: afghanistan → colombia (approximately 50 countries)
countries covered batch 2: comoros → guyana (approximately 30 countries)
countries covered batch 3: haiti → kuwait (approximately 25 countries)

remaining: approximately 110 UN member states not yet covered
